questions.question: What ingredients does a CSS transition need?
questions.answer: A start value, an end value, a transitionable property, a duration, and a trigger (hover, focus, class change). Optional timing function and delay shape the motion.

questions.question: Why prefer transform and opacity for animation?
questions.answer: They can be handled by the compositor without triggering layout or paint, so they stay smooth. Animating width, height, top, or left forces layout/paint on each frame.

questions.question: What does transform-origin change?
questions.answer: It sets the pivot point for rotation and scaling (default center). Changing it makes an element scale or rotate from a corner or edge.

questions.question: Where do perspective and transform-style belong for a 3D flip?
questions.answer: perspective goes on the parent to define viewing depth. transform-style: preserve-3d goes on the element whose children should keep their 3D positions, usually the inner flipping element.

questions.question: How do you respect prefers-reduced-motion?
questions.answer: Wrap non-essential animations/transitions in @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) and disable or shorten them. Keep essential state changes instant and avoid large motion.

questions.question: Create a card that lifts 4px and scales 2% on hover with a 180ms ease transition.
Why is transition: all risky?
questions.answer: It animates every changing property, including expensive layout properties and ones you did not intend, causing jank and surprising effects. List the properties explicitly.

questions.question: Why does a transform sometimes blur text or create unexpected stacking?
questions.answer: Scale can rasterize text at fractional sizes, and any transform creates a stacking context and containing block. That changes z-index ordering and fixed/absolute positioning inside it.
